summary: xAI launched Grok Bot, a beta product giving users autonomous AI agents that operate their own cloud computer to complete multi-step tasks across apps and tools, coordinate with other agents, and learn workflows over time.

mechanisms.reason: The product explicitly reframes the unit of work from a human using software to an always-on agent that finishes tasks end-to-end across apps and only returns for approval, the core definition of the agentic workflow shift.
mechanisms.quote: Grok Bot is your team of always-on agents. They have their own computer, work inside tools and apps like you do, and keep working 24/7.

mechanisms.reason: Running multiple parallel, always-on agents per user that coordinate with each other implies materially more inference calls issued per task than a single-prompt interaction.
mechanisms.quote: People inside SpaceXAI often run multiple Bots in parallel, with one to manage the others.

practices.reason: The described chief-of-staff-plus-specialist multi-agent pattern with shared threads and group-chat coordination is a concrete architecture an engineering team could evaluate for its own agent orchestration, though no quantitative gain is given.
practices.quote: A chief of staff sits on top, with a specialist for each lane: inbox management, expenses, recruiting, bug fixes, or operations.

practices.reason: Learning a workflow by observation and replaying it as a saved routine is a workable pattern for reducing re-prompting, but it is described only anecdotally with no methodology or metric.
practices.quote: It saves your workflow as a routine, takes your corrections, and runs it on its own next time, so you can hand off the same multi-step process without re-explaining it again.

notable_reason: A frontier lab shipping a full agent-as-teammate product that operates its own computer across arbitrary apps is a concrete, shipping instance of the seat-to-agent displacement trend rather than a claim about it.
